steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What happened...? What's with all the empty bottles on the floor?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Odd. Why was I even sleeping here?

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Rosalind... you're a good kid...

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: ...Arctosz... you... disgrace...

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: (Snore)

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Dad?!

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Eh? Uh…

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: What did you wake me up for?! Can't an old man nap in peace?!

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: No, hold on, I...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Dad? When did you get home? Why didn't you let me know you were coming?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What happened yesterday? How did we end up sleeping on the floor?

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Quit your yapping, it's giving me a headache.

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: Sir, Master.

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: I'm so glad you're both finally awake!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Gulo!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What happened here?

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: The two of you got drunk, and didn't want to stop drinking, and our efforts to convince you to return to your rooms to sleep were in vain.

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: I could only feed two more batches of firewood to the furnace so it wouldn't get too cold in here.

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: Sir, do you not remember what happened yesterday?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I... Wait, let me think.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Yesterday, yesterday...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I remember. I was to prepare for the banquet to celebrate the completion of Kjeragandr's statue.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: The Saintess asked me to select the best drinks Kjerag has to offer, so I was tasting them one by one...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: And then, after that... I don't remember much.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Hmph, of course you don't.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: You were so drunk you couldn't tell people apart, and even tried to toast to a pillar while hugging it.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: At your age! What an embarrassment!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Enough, Dad. Was I not doing it for the Saintess, for Kjerag?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Gulo's still here, so could you ease up on the scolding, before I lose any more respect!

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: I always taught you respect is something you earn on your own, so why ask me to leave any for you?!

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Forget it, I'll bicker with you no longer.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Gulo, where's Rosalind?

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: She went up the mountain first thing in the morning, Master.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: She woke up early, while the both of you were still sleeping, and she said to let you sleep a while longer.

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: I thought the same, so I didn't wake you.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: I guess it's fine for her to just leave like that.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Perhaps this was Kjeragandr's plan for the Paleroches.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: They met, they didn't realize, so I guess this means it was just not meant to be... indeed...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What are you riddling about now, Dad?!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I vaguely remember a young girl coming here yesterday, but I did drink too much. I can't remember what she looked like.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You say her name was Rosalind? Hmm...

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Arctosz, come here.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: I should not hide this from you.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Same as you made your own choice back then.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: What should be done next, is ultimately up to you.

steps.name: Guard?
steps.text: ...By Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Guard?
steps.text: Three generations really drank the night away.

steps.name: Guard?
steps.text: Even dragged me in with the other guards too.

steps.name: Guard?
steps.text: Ghh—

steps.name: Guard?
steps.text: It's been a long time since I drank so much.

steps.name: Guard?
steps.text: And I didn't get any business done at all...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: ...Since going roundabout didn't work, let's just go head-on.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Judging from the direction, Rosalind probably went up the mountain.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Ohh—This is one of those snowy mountains!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It's even more spectacular up close. Kjerag's mountains sure are impressive.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Ugh, I'm a little dizzy. Really went overboard on the drinks last night.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Wonder if those guys are awake yet. Why didn't the Doctor tell me how enthusiastic Kjerag people can be?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I should give them something as thanks when I get down the mountain later...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Sheesh, it's freezing. The wind's pretty painful.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: If I remember right... you're supposed to climb up this mountain on your own to prove your faith to Kjeragandr?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It's really tall.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: But since I'm already here, I might as well try.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: The purest air from up in the mountains?

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: Sounds pretty good to me. Do you take cards here?

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: Alright, then give me two boxes. Send them to the Burdenpeak Hotel, room 606.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: You got it!

steps.name: Foreign Tourist B
steps.text: Woah, Zofia... you're buying even more stuff.

steps.name: Foreign Tourist B
steps.text: Didn't you buy four boxes of mountain spring water yesterday? How are we going to bring it all back?

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: Don't be silly! Who says we have to bring them home ourselves?

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: I'll send a box each to Młynar and Margaret. I probably haven't even bought enough yet.

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: Kjerag's air and water are plenty impressive. The Black Knight came here a good long while ago, so she should be living pretty well now.

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: Alright, enough of that. I hear you have to climb Kjerag's mountains yourself, as a show of devotion.

steps.name: Foreign Tourist A
steps.text: Come on! Let's get climbing!

steps.name: Foreign Tourist B
steps.text: They do mention as much in the travel brochure.

steps.name: Foreign Tourist B
steps.text: Let's see who can reach the summit first, Zofia!

steps.name: Kjerag Youth
steps.text: Riley, why didn't you tell them we have a cable car that goes up the mountain?

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: Hohoho. The tourists have their own ideas, who am I to tell them otherwise?

steps.name: Kjerag Youth
steps.text: Fair enough...

steps.name: Kjerag Youth
steps.text: Seems like tourists are the only ones who like to climb these days.

steps.name: Kjerag Youth
steps.text: They're right though.

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: Come! Let's go take the cable car!

steps.name: Kjerag Youth
steps.text: Really? Won't Kjeragandr see it as a lack of faith?

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: Nonsense! Kjeragandr granted us this convenience because She loves Her people!

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: Insisting on climbing would show a lack of faith in Kjeragandr!

steps.name: Kjerag Youth
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: What do you mean, 'huh?'

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: We're all Kjeragandr's children. As long as you respect Her and keep Her in your heart, She'll protect us all!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Whew. You can actually ride a cable car up the mountain?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Why are tourist spots the same everywhere...? I'd better follow the locals.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Even though I don't know what it means to have faith in Kjeragandr at all.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: But Kjeragandr must be protecting Kjerag, judging by how things are going?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey, old man in front!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Can you tell me where to get cable car tickets? Thanks for pointing the way!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Sir, please hold on.

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: Who are you? What's with the getup?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I'm a reporter from Victoria, you see.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: People praise the Kjeragandr statue, but surely building it must have been a waste of resources. I'm currently collecting some—

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: Get lost!

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: My son who works on the statue sends me money every month, and even calls me to tell me how good work is over there.

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: You foreigners are just salty about how wonderful our Kjerag is!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Then, why hasn't he returned?

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: He said he signed some agreement, so he has to stay there.

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: What was it again?

steps.name: Kjerag Youth
steps.text: Non-disclosure.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Do you need an NDA to build a statue?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: I'm warning you, foreigner. Any more guff out of you and I'll give you a taste of my walking stick.

steps.name: Kjerag Elder
steps.text: Huh? Where'd they go?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Hm~ Hmm-hmm-hm~ Praise Kjeragandr...♪

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Brave Burdenbeasts~ Brave people~ Kjeragandr guides us~ To protect our homeland, hm hmm~♪

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Hmm, Hm-hm-hmm...♪

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Huh? The snow here doesn't seem right...

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Yow!
Careful.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There's a trap down there.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You alright?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Oh, Madam Degenbrecher!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Where did this hole come from...? That Riley must have dug it out to catch game!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Many, many thanks. I would have fallen down the hole, if it weren't for you.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're welcome.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Do you have business on the mountain today, Madam?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Anything we can help you with? I have plans with Riley, Leone, and the other guys to go up the mountain today, so just let us know if you need anything!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I have a bit of work to do, but I'll be fine on my own.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Are you and Old Riley still drinking with the Victorians?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Yeah, we've been competing to see who can drink more, and it's a tie, at the moment!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: None of us are giving up, because it'd be an embarrassment for Master Enciodes and the Saintess if we lost to those Victorians!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Also, they just suddenly came in here and set up camp. What do you think is going on?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: I've no proper education, but even I know a sudden flood of people here, all hale and healthy even, can't possibly be a good thing!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: That's why Riley and I were thinking we could keep an eye on them for Sir Enciodes with the drinking, at the very least.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: So don't worry. We'll definitely win!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Fine, it would be great if you could drink till they puke.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Just call me if you can't. Don't push yourselves.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Did you decide to watch the Victorians on your own?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Hehe, we thought it up with the other villagers. All of us agreed to it!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: We've been living much better these days, and since we now know how good things can be, we're not gonna let anyone ruin it for us.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: But Madam, I should be honest with you, just don't get angry with me.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Sure, go on.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: I just wanted to say, these Victorians we've been drinking with.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: We've come to know them pretty well over the past month, and brushing the other stuff aside, they aren't bad guys.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: They don't cause too much trouble, even when drunk, and sometimes they come over to help out with work.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: There's a guy with bones about as old as mine. He only goes a little mad when he's drunk, but he doesn't do much other than strip off his clothes to try and swim in the snow. I saw his back then, it was in bad shape.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: I don't know what he has suffered, but it hurts to even look at. It hurts to think about now.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I might as well tell you this.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: A Victorian Viscount has come to join the celebrations for Kjeragandr's statue, and he's brought his personal army along.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Most of them are veterans who have been fighting alongside him for a long time.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There's no need to think too much, just enjoy your drinks together.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: *sigh* I don't get it, what's the difference between a personal and regular army?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: But they did look far from young, and a few of them seem to have stones growing on their bodies.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: That should be the uh, stone disease, I've seen in the news before?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: ...Oripathy.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Most of the time, nothing happens when you come into contact with it, so you needn't be too worried.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: But you should still take some precautions.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You can go to Rhodes Island's office in the city or the newly built hospital for information on how to protect yourself.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: That we know, so don't you worry, Madam.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: I just wanted to have a chat with you anyways. I wouldn't dare to disturb Sir Enciodes or Sir Gnosis.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're saying I look idle?

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: That's not what I meant!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: I mean, them Sirs are busy with their big projects all day long, so it'd be no good for us to disturb them.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: You help us out regularly, even though you're so busy too. We know you're on the same side as us. You're one of us!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: One of you...

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Wait, no. I mean, those Sirs are our people too.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: I'm bad with words, but you know what I mean!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Am I wasting your time, Madam?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There's something I need to trouble you and the rest on the mountain for.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Just say the word!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Help me find a pretentious Victorian.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: A what?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: He wears a top hat and a black coat with the collar covering his face. Some gemstones too.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's easy to spot such a conspicuous figure.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: What's this fella doing with that sort of outfit in Kjerag?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Who knows?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Probably something stupid.

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: Alright, leave it to us!

steps.name: Carefree Villager
steps.text: I'll send over Old Leones' Burdenbeast the moment we get any news!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Are you serious, Dad?!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: The girl yesterday... She's, she's Rosalind? My daughter?!

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: ...Sigh.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: I doubt I'm wrong. The girl looks just like you, and Tatyana too.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: My eyes are still good enough, I'm not wrong.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Really...?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: My... daughter...?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Hahaha! I did say she was a good kid! Good stature, and character even! Wonderful!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Rosalind, Rosalind... She looks like me?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Yes, like me, I remember now. She has the same hair color!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Her eyes and mouth are Tatyana's, especially her eyes... they're exactly the same! So pretty...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: ...Time flies. Little Rosalind has already grown so big, in just the blink of an eye...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Wait, did she go up the mountain?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: When is she coming back? Will she come back?

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Arctosz, there's something else...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: We can talk about that later. I have to prepare some gifts for my daughter!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I remember she loved baked sweet cheese and beast stew, when she was little, so I'm off to buy some now!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Tatyana... is she here too? Does she not want to see me? Then I, I...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Alright! No matter, I'll head straight up the mountain and give them to Rosalind!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: And then I'll ask her about Tatyana...

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Arctosz!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What is it?! I need to hurry—

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Stop right there!

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: ...Just. Stay. You need to hear this.
Arctosz stops in his tracks from his father's yelling, and an ill omen stirs uncontrollably in his heart.
Perhaps it's his hangover, but a sudden headache descends on him, his stomach seems to drop to the floor, and his back feels as if something cold is creeping up on him.
Only now does Arctosz realize his father's back, which he has not seen in a long time, is slightly stooped, like a wilting tree, no longer tall and upright as he remembered.
But the dry and aged voice of the devotee continues, undeterred by Arctosz's panic.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Rosalind told me she and her mother had been living in Ursus since they left.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: She was too young to remember anything of this place.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: She said she never knew who her father was, all the time she grew up.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: And this time she's here not only to see our Kjeragandr's statue, but also...

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: She's brought back her mother's remains.
Ill omens always seem to bear out.
The wind and snow roaring outside their home, the flames flickering inside the furnace, and even their indistinguishable breathing all seem to freeze for a moment.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Remains...?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: B-But, Tatyana was so young. How could she...?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I don't believe it... how can that be...?

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: I heard it from the girl myself.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: What happened back then... it was Clan Paleroche that failed mother and daughter.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: I carry the shame in my heart, but not regret.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: What about you, Arctosz?

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Fine, it doesn't matter what you want to say. There's no point telling me.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: Your father is no perfect man, nor a saint, and certainly not the victim here.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: This old man is too old to hear you out, let alone offer any advice.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: I only wish to spend the rest of my days sweeping the dust at Kjeragandr's feet.

steps.name: Elder Devotee
steps.text: But you... should think carefully.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Tatyana... Rosalind...

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: Sir, Master!

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: Matriarch Ratatos is here, she says there's something urgent to discuss!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Ugh. The place reeks of booze...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: The ceremony's tomorrow, Arctosz. Don't you drink too much and ruin it all.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I'm in no mood to play with you.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Just tell me what happened. You're not the type to make social calls, Ratatos.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Heheh, you sure know me well.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Fine, I'll get straight to the point, Arctosz. I came here to tip you off.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I still recall that you married an Ursine woman, despite your family's objections, and even had a child with her?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Something happened to the Silverashes, and soon after your wife left Kjerag with daughter in tow. This affair was kept within the tri-clans, but it was no secret to us.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Hmph, I see your nose is as sharp as ever.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I'll take that as a compliment.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I'm here to tell you about your daughter, the girl named Rosalind.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What happened to her?! You better not be taking advantage the situation!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: She has nothing to do with our clan business!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I'm not here to settle any old scores, but her untimely return is really unfortunate.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Do you know where she is right now?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: She's probably already in the sights of a Victorian spy.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Finally!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: But the cable car only goes up this far, and I have to climb the rest myself?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Well, the summit isn't that far anyway.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I could still see a few tourists earlier, but now there's no one else around.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: White everywhere... Sheesh, it's a little scary.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Huh...?
...How... unlucky...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Wh-What was that?
...Ever since I came to Kjerag... Not a single thing has gone smoothly...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Who's that? C-Come out! Don't even think you can scare me!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Is that... a hole?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Who could be so bored as to dig a hole by the trail? No, this can't be just a hole...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It's a trap!
Sure enough. A trap indeed.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Watch your step, Madam.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Also, if it's not too much of a bother, could I trouble you to pull me up?
